_: Ceilings for UniChat on CI devices (scripts/mobile-perf.mjs), one set per profile. android: API 35, google_apis, x86_64 with KVM, the release APK of the production config built with UNICHAT_PERF_MARKS=1; every PR that reaches the binary measures apkMB, coldStartTtidMs, coldStartJsBootMs and coldStartFirstScreenMs (mobile-verify.yml › android-smoke); the nightly measures coldStartInboxMs, scrollJankyPercent, scrollP90FrameMs and memoryPssMB with the staging account (chat-mobile-verify.yml › android). android-2gb: the same APK on API 35 with 2 GB of RAM, the low-end leg of the nightly matrix (chat-mobile-verify.yml › android-matrix). ios-simulator: the Release simulator build, timed to the marks it writes to its documents (mobile-verify.yml › ios-release). A profile listed in `provisional` still has the ceilings set 2026-10-22 before any run measured this app: they catch a gross regression (a doubled start, a frozen scroll), not a small one. After five green runs of its job, `node scripts/mobile-perf.mjs tighten --profile <name> --write <the runs' unichat-perf-* files>` sets each ceiling to the worst run + 15 % (the emulator is noisy) and takes the profile off the list, in one commit that quotes the runs; then they only go down, and one goes up only in the commit that adds the weight, saying why. The emulator renders without a GPU: frame numbers are for comparison between builds, not a claim about a phone.
